title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity for streaming, tools, structured output, and params
author: Priya Patel
description: Summary: Implements parity for the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions surface across the hosted compatibility layer and runtime plumbing. This PR unifies parameter handling (roles, stop sequences, logprobs, max_tokens), stabilizes streaming behavior for chunked responses and function/tool-calling streaming, and improves structured-output/JSON candidates handling. Motivation: customers rely on OpenAI-compatible endpoints for migration; missing or divergent semantics around roles, stop/logprobs, and streaming function call payloads caused subtle regressions and interop issues. This change reduces customer friction and aligns behavior with common SDKs and downstream evaluation harnesses. Changes (high level): - Compatibility layer parsing: normalize OpenAI-style message role mapping (system|user|assistant|tool) and accept both "role" strings and numeric enums from older clients. - stop parameter: support list and string variants, exact-match vs token-prefix behavior configurable via compatibility flag; documented default is exact-match to match OpenAI historical behavior. - logprobs: wire through per-token logprob outputs from the runtime when available; add graceful fallback (null) when backend model doesn't provide logprobs. - max_tokens and response truncation: enforce compatibility semantics for max_tokens vs model max context; add explicit truncate_reason field in streaming events. - Streaming: stabilize chunk boundaries by emitting a deterministic "delta" stream with explicit event types (response.delta, response.final, response.tool_call.start/arg/finish) and optional partial function call payloads for consumers that stream tool arguments. Backpressure and connection-close semantics improved to ensure no lost tool-call data on client disconnect. - Function/tool calling: route function call candidates as structured objects in the compatibility payload and support streaming of arguments. - Structured output: add heuristics for JSON-candidate extraction and a new header in the compatibility envelope to mark trusted structured outputs; add confidence metadata when available. - Tests and examples: new integration tests in redwood-openai-compat, updated python/typescript SDK examples showing compatibility flags and streaming tool-call usage. Migration notes: - Default behavior aims to be compatible with common OpenAI client expectations; teams relying on previous Redwood-specific behavior should opt into the legacy compatibility flag (compat.openai.strict=false) to preserve older semantics. - logprobs will only be present when backends are able to produce them; clients should check presence before indexing. Rollout plan: staged canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) behind a feature flag; compatibility mode enabled by default for the hosted openai route. See ENG-4521 for rollout gating. Testing: unit tests for parsing/mapping, e2e with streaming harness (perf-canary), and several cross-SDK compatibility scenarios. CI history: an intermittent streaming test failed in the first run due to an off-by-one chunk boundary; fixed in the second commit and CI passed. Related: parallels earlier work on structured output extraction (ENG-4387) and streaming stabilization (ENG-4410).

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Overall looks good. Please add a note in the docs about clients that rely on prefix-based stop matching. Also confirm performance impact of the deterministic emitter on throughput.
Priya Patel (author): Answered: added docs note and benchmarked emitter overhead (~2% median latency on our canary model); included results in observability dashboard.
Clara Zhang: Request change: line-delimited streaming events need strict JSON envelope validation to avoid client-side parser errors. Can we emit a length-prefixed envelope for the critical events?

Priya Patel (author): Replied: implemented an optional length-prefixed mode behind compat flag openai.stream_length_prefix=true; default remains line-delimited for backwards compatibility. Added tests.
Aaron Kim: Approving smoke tests, but please add a regression test for logprobs missing from some backends (null handling).
Priya Patel (author): Added test 'logprobs_roundtrip.test.go' to ensure graceful null handling.
Emma Liu: Verified docs example in SDKs and ran the typescript example against staging; streaming function args were reassembled correctly. Approved.

release_notes: Added OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility: normalized roles, list/string stop handling, streamed function/tool call support, logprobs passthrough when available, stabilized streaming event types, and improved structured-output extraction. Backwards-compatibility flags available for teams that rely on prior behavior.
notes_for_release_engineering: Rollout staged via feature flag (openai.compat_parity) — coordinate canary with infra, monitor openai_compat_metrics and streaming error traces. If issues arise, flip compat.openai.strict=false to revert to legacy behavior for affected customers.
test_matrix_summary: Unit tests for mapping/parsing, integration e2e for streaming tool calls, SDK example verification (python/ts), and perf-canary to measure emitter overhead.
